Subject: RE: Intermittent auth failures during checkout — impact and credit request

Quick technical summary (initial):
- Alert at ~2028-07-24 08:46:12 UTC: increased 502/503 responses from auth-proxy layer for customers routed to aus-2 host group
- Automated fallback attempted but a misconfigured token-bucket on the authz cache caused per-host queueing; a small percentage of requests returned 502s instead of being retried successfully
- Error window we observe in our traces: 08:45:57 UTC — 09:09:58 UTC (24m 1s). Peak error rate between 08:52—08:58 UTC (6m)
- Root cause hypothesis: regression in recent config roll (auth-cache throttling param) that reduced headroom under sudden retry storms

Attachments: redwood-traces-07-24-08-45-09-10.tar.gz (log bundle, 42MB)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Reconcile your trace IDs with ours (please send the trace ids from your side)
2) We’ll run the SLO eligibility check against the availability window. Early read: this looks like it could qualify as an availability incident per section 2.1 of our SLA because the error window exceeds the configured threshold for your class of service.
3) Prepare post-incident RCA and mitigation plan (canary guardrail update + rollback of throttling adjustment)

I’ll follow up with a short executive summary we can share externally.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
